{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Robert Hamilton Austin''' (born 1946) is an American physicist and a professor of physics at [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&q=Robert+Hamilton+Austin&btnG=&as_sdt=1%2C44&as_sdtp= |title=Robert Hamilton Austin |accessdate=July 1, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Robert H. Austin|url=https://austingroup.princeton.edu/people/robert-h-austin|website=austingroup.princeton.edu|language=en|access-date=2020-05-14}}</ref>

== Life ==

He was born in St. Charles, Illinois in 1946.<ref name="aps.org">{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Robert&last_nm=Austin&year=2005|title=Prize Recipient|work=aps.org|accessdate=11 March 2017}}</ref>

He received his BA in 1968 from Hope College. He received his M.S. and Ph.D. in physics from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.<ref name="aps.org"/> His current work concerns biological systems evolution and the research behind it.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.princeton.edu/physics/people/display_person.xml?netid=austin |title=Robert Austin |publisher=princeton.edu |accessdate=July 1, 2017}}</ref>

== Career ==

He is currently professor of physics at Princeton University.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://austingroup.princeton.edu |title=Robert H. Austin Lab |publisher=princeton.edu |accessdate=July 1, 2017}}</ref><ref name="aps.org"/>

He is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (1988)<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1988&unit_id=&institution=Princeton+University}}</ref> and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. He was elected as a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1999 and a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Robert Austin|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/robert-h-austin-7r0hqr/|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2020-05-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Robert Hamilton Austin|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/robert-hamilton-austin|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en|access-date=2020-05-14}}</ref>

In 2005, he received the [[Julius Edgar Lilienfeld Prize]].
